title: Stability of Thy Times
summary: A constructive, mildly hawkish hold that walks back the Jul 9 re-hardening. In prepared remarks at the Partnership for New York City, Williams calls inflation 'unquestionably too high at about 4 percent' and says it is 'imperative' to restore 2%, but the speech's center of gravity is a six-part case that inflation HAS PEAKED: tariff direct effects largely played out (new tariffs mostly replacing expiring ones), shelter disinflation intact, energy prices likely peaked with futures pointing back toward pre-Hormuz-closure levels, AI supply-demand imbalances receding as supply comes online, no labor-market inflation pressure (HPW index, wage growth consistent with low inflation), and anchored expectations. He publishes a full glide path: inflation ~3-1/4% by year-end, toward 2% in 2027, on target in 2028, with growth 2-2-1/4% (modestly above potential) and unemployment edging DOWN to 4% by 2028. The labor market is 'solid and stable' with prior warning signs 'largely stabilized, albeit at low levels.' Policy is 'well positioned' at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4%, with a data-dependent, totality-of-the-data close and no hint of either a cut or the hike scenario he spelled out on Jul 9 — the AI-demand impulse he then said one 'doesn't look through' is now framed as receding over time, though 'highly uncertain' in magnitude and duration. Net: a step back down from the Jul 9 hawkish edge to roughly his Jul 7 stance — patient hold, inflation still the binding concern, but with a firmer disinflation call.

key_quotes.quote: Inflation is unquestionably too high at about 4 percent, well above the FOMC's longer-run goal of 2 percent.
key_quotes.context: Inflation remains the binding concern and the reason for the hold

key_quotes.quote: But there are encouraging reasons to expect that inflation has peaked and should edge down in coming quarters.
key_quotes.context: The headline marginal shift: an explicit inflation-has-peaked call backed by six reasons (tariffs played out, shelter, energy futures, AI supply, labor, anchored expectations)

key_quotes.quote: The current stance of monetary policy is well positioned to do that.
key_quotes.context: Reaffirms the 3-1/2 to 3-3/4% hold as appropriately calibrated; no easing signal, and none of the Jul 9 hike-scenario language

key_quotes.quote: Fourth, the supply-demand imbalances stemming from AI-related investment should recede over time as more supply comes online. That said, the magnitude and duration of these supply-demand imbalances are highly uncertain.
key_quotes.context: Softens the Jul 9 framing in which the AI demand impulse was his MAIN inflation concern and something you 'don't look through' — now listed among the reasons inflation edges down

key_quotes.quote: I expect overall inflation to decline to around 3-1/4 percent by year-end, then continue on a glide path toward our 2 percent goal in 2027 and land on target in 2028.
key_quotes.context: A published forecast path consistent with a long patient hold rather than hikes

key_quotes.quote: Fifth, we do not see evidence of the labor market adding to inflationary pressures.
key_quotes.context: Labor solid and stable, prior warning signs 'largely stabilized, albeit at low levels' — neither a reason to ease nor an inflation worry
